cells.tense: The pushing is happening now, and the hands are on it.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Take one thing the tradition does without anyone saying why, trace how it actually works onto a page, and follow that page instead of the habit.
cells.core:
You force change on things that hold people, and it holds because you don't rush. Where a custom, a ritual, a way of doing things has gotten in the way, you move it in your own time and the moved version stays moved. That is rare, and it can look like stubbornness from outside, but the structures that stay up afterward are the ones you put up carefully.

The pattern reads clearly enough that people bring you the fixable thing and let you fix it. Before the next one, take something the tradition does without anyone saying why, trace how it actually works onto a page, and follow that instead of the habit. The habit will keep tugging. The page will show you where the working actually sat.
cells.sheetLine: You move what holds people, slowly, and it stays moved.
cells.verb: forcing structural change into reality, slow and unstoppable

cells.tense: Tomorrow it will already be rebuilt, and tomorrow is where you are living.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Find one person who already shares this with you, and do the next piece of the work beside them rather than ahead of them.
cells.core:
The rebuilding has run out in front of the room. You can already see the finished version, so you are halfway into it while the people it is for are still at the table, and the push that used to wait for the ground to be ready is now arriving first. The plans are bright. What stands between your version and theirs is where the force is going.

The fix is not less force, it is company. Find one person who already shares this with you, and do the next piece of the work beside them — hands on it together, no briefing, no catching-up. Any structure this place keeps standing is held up by people being in it with you. Build where someone is standing, not where you will be standing.
cells.sheetLine: You are building from a place the others haven't reached yet.
cells.verb: forcing structural change into reality, slow and unstoppable

cells.tense: That door is behind you, and you are still facing it.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Wait for the next moment when something here is plainly out of place, then change that one thing alone and say nothing about it.
cells.core:
The push has been waiting for permission too long. There was a moment when the old shape could have been moved, and now the room has settled around it, and the hands that once moved it stay where they are. The custom decides things, and you follow it more easily than you once would have, and the following is what the young ones copy.

Start smaller than the original problem. Wait for the next moment when something here is plainly out of place, then change that one thing alone and say nothing about it. It will not feel like enough. It does not need to feel like enough — it needs to show that the pushing still works when the hand is yours.
cells.sheetLine: Things get decided for you now, and you go along.
cells.verb: forcing structural change into reality, slow and unstoppable

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are still writing.
cells.act: tend the fire without burning out
cells.ask: Keep caring for the piece of this that still matters, a little at a time, and ask nothing back from it.
cells.core:
The pushing is happening, and it has been happening under another name. You will say the tradition runs itself or the group keeps it steady, while the actual moving — the part that keeps a rite alive, that decides what gets carried and what gets let go — sits in hands that say they are just keeping up. The work is steady and patient and it looks like upkeep from the inside.

Underneath is care that hasn't said its name. Keep caring for the piece of this that still matters, a little at a time, and ask nothing back from it. The care doesn't need to enlarge into a speech. It needs somewhere to go.
cells.sheetLine: You say you're keeping up, and the moving is yours.
cells.verb: forcing structural change into reality, slow and unstoppable

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that pushing structure is what isolates this person — the record shows the capacity, not its social cost. A reader could say the push isn't forceful but careful, or that it isn't happening at all. The asks survive being wrong because each is small, done in a week, and teaches something about how the capacity actually moves. The sentence serving the writer is 'Mostly what happens is people leave' — it wants to be seen more than it wants to be useful.
